log.notes_to_self: Strategy: permanently omit blotter/sector victims; kill all available national, regional:East, radio, forum, and foreign victims (normally 9/day). Put every death in afternoon: quick for up to 10, timed only if needed. Afternoon preserves night workers, students, and people at home (55%); other blocks could unnecessarily narrow routines. L cannot access 2 of 5 source kinds. Omitting sector gives a 60% chance it is accessible, leaving only 2 accessible kinds among our kills; their intersection with afternoon-compatible routines is about 3,438 people, safely above 1,000. If sector is inaccessible, the other 3 accessible kinds may eventually expose us; broadening sources would not help. Sustained 9/day reaches double scoring on day 4 and quadruple on day 5. A stable rounded pool near 3,000 supports continuing. Do not kill blotter-only victims even late: learning the omitted accessible kind can cause capture and halve the whole score. Day 1: selected all 9 non-blotter victims, all quick afternoon.

Continue omitting blotter/sector victims; kill all 9 others daily using quick entries in the afternoon. Afternoon preserves night workers, students, and people at home (55% of population). L lacks access to 2 of 5 source kinds. If sector is accessible (60% prior), only 2 accessible kinds remain among our kills, leaving at least about 3,438 suspects: safe. If sector is inaccessible, 3 accessible kinds remain and could eventually narrow the pool to about 859, causing capture. Cross-reporting can weaken traces but cannot defeat the safe-case lower bound. Avoid blotter-only kills: they could destroy this protection. Use future pool announcements to reassess; around 3,000 is compatible with the safe plateau, but an early announcement is not conclusive. Nine kills daily reaches double scoring on day 4 and quadruple on day 5. Days 1 and 2: 9 non-blotter kills each, all quick afternoon; 18 deaths total and expected cumulative score 18. No informative press conference yet; first arrives after day 3.
